QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_12

question.text: At a board meeting, the CEO of Chambal Managed Futures Fund cites the scale of the Indian AIF industry. Per Section 4.5 of the chapter, which datapoint is CORRECT as of the reporting dates cited?

answer.text: 150 AIFs registered with SEBI and INR 1 lakh crore in commitments
1,765 AIFs registered with SEBI (as on Feb 4, 2026) and capital commitments surpassing INR 15.74 lakh crore (as on Dec 31, 2026)
500 AIFs registered and INR 50 lakh crore in commitments, starting from 100 AIFs in 2012
1,765 AIFs registered and INR 1.5 lakh crore in commitments, flat since 2012

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 4.5 states: 'As on February 4, 2026, 1,765 AIFs were registered with SEBI. Starting with just 21 funds in 2012, the industry has seen a high growth in terms of number of registered AIFs. Capital commitments raised by all registered AIFs (across categories) have surpassed INR 15.74 lakh crore as on December 31, 2026.' This captures the 14-year growth arc. The Trap: Option A under-counts. Option C wrongly claims 100 starting funds (it was 21) and inflates commitments. Option D drops a decimal on commitments and denies growth. Cross-Exam Context: Every AIF exam (XIX-A through XIX-E) tests these headline numbers; they refresh each NISM workbook cycle. Memorise 1,765 / INR 15.74 lakh crore / 21 starter funds for the current cycle.
